speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures, lethargy, and neurological signs three days after birth. To understand the cause of your symptoms, I need to know if your mother had a fever during pregnancy or delivery, and if you were exposed to any infections. REQUEST TEST: Maternal_serology_and_viral_panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The maternal serology and viral panel results are normal, which helps rule out certain congenital infections. Given your neonate's seizures and lethargy, have you noticed any abnormal movements or breathing patterns specifically in the last 24 hours? REQUEST TEST: Blood_glucose_and_arterial_blood_gas.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Glucose: Hypoglycemic (25 mg/dL); Arterial Blood Gas: pH 7.28, pCO2 55 mm Hg, pO2 65 mm Hg, HCO3 22 mEq/L, Base Deficit 4 mEq/L

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood glucose is critically low at 25 mg/dL, and the arterial blood gas indicates respiratory acidosis with a pH of 7.28. These findings suggest hypoglycemia and potential metabolic acidosis are driving your neurological symptoms. REQUEST TEST: Serum_ammonia_and_lactate.

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI.

Have you or your family noticed any symptoms of metabolic disorders, such as poor feeding or failure to thrive, prior to this admission?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum Ammonia: Elevated; Lactate: Elevated. Brain MRI: Shows signs of intraventricular hemorrhage with associated periventricular leukomalacia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of seizures, lethargy, hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and now elevated ammonia and lactate alongside intraventricular hemorrhage and periventricular leukomalacia on MRI strongly suggests a severe inborn error of metabolism, likely organic acidemia or fatty acid oxidation disorder, potentially complicated by the hemorrhage. Did you have any family history of sudden infant death, unexplained coma, or siblings with similar metabolic issues? REQUEST TEST: Plasma_amino_acids_and_urine_organoacids.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Plasma Amino Acids: Elevated leucine, isoleucine, valine, and methionine; Urine Organ Acids: Elevated 3-hydroxyisovalerate and 3-methylglutaconic acid

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) combined with elevated 3-hydroxyisovalerate in the urine are diagnostic for Maple Syrup Urine Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Maple Syrup Urine Disease (Branched-Chain Ketoaciduria).
